module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 63

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

## Counterexample

The conjecture is false for the lexicographic product $C_5[K_4]$. This graph
has minimum even-distance count $9$, while its largest induced forest and
largest induced bipartite subgraph both have order $4$. The conjectured lower
bound is therefore $\lceil(9 + 4 + 1)/3\rceil = 5 > 4$.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture63

open SimpleGraph

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 63](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
asked whether every simple connected graph $G$ satisfies
$f(G) \geq \lceil(\min_v \operatorname{distEven}(v) + b(G) + 1)/3\rceil$.
The answer is no, as witnessed by $C_5[K_4]$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
"https://github.com/Kuberwastaken/wowii-63-85-counterexample/blob/cba739842ec59adf7426c180009175b31935701d/lean/WOWII63.lean#L184-L195"]
theorem conjecture63 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]
      (G : SimpleGraph α) (_h : G.Connected),
      let minDistEven := (Finset.univ.image (G.distEven ·)).min' (by simp)
      ⌈((minDistEven : ℝ) + G.b + 1) / 3⌉ ≤ (G.largestInducedForestSize : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/-- Every vertex is counted among the vertices at even distance from itself. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) (v : Fin 3) : 0 < G.distEven v := by
  unfold SimpleGraph.distEven
  apply Finset.card_pos.mpr
  exact ⟨v, Finset.mem_filter.mpr
    ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, ⟨0, by simp [SimpleGraph.dist_self]⟩⟩⟩

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture63

reformulations.difference: The right-hand side quantifies only over vertex types with `[Nontrivial α]` (at least two vertices). The source says "If G is a simple connected graph", which also covers the one-vertex graph K1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: `G.Connected` already forces a nonempty vertex type. A nonempty type that is not nontrivial has exactly one element, so the graph is K1. For K1: min dist_even = 1 (v itself, at distance 0), b = 1 and f = 1, so the bound is ⌈(1+1+1)/3⌉ = 1 ≤ 1. The excluded case satisfies the inequality, so restricting to nontrivial types does not change the truth value of the universal claim. In a scratch file I proved `rhs_iff_source`: the file's right-hand side ↔ the same inequality over all `[Nonempty α]` finite types with `G.Connected`. The helper lemma `ineq63_of_unique` proves the inequality for every graph on a `Unique` type.

review.notes: No misformalization found. What I checked: (1) The source statement matches exactly: 'If G is a simple connected graph, then f(G) ≥ CEIL[(minimum of dist_even(v) + b(G) + 1)/3]'. (2) All definitions match the WOWII glossary. dist_even(v) is 'the number of vertices whose distance from v is an even integer', so v is counted, as in `SimpleGraph.distEven`. With the other convention the counterexample would still work (⌈13/3⌉ = 5 > 4). (3) The external proof (Kuberwastaken/wowii-63-85-counterexample@cba7398, lines 184–195) states the identical theorem. I recompiled it with the import pointed at this module and the current repository definitions, and it goes through. It depends on `native_decide` auxiliary axioms (the kernel trusts compiled code), which the external README acknowledges. The formal-conjectures revision it pins (e751934) differs in Induced.lean only by dropping `open Classical` and adding lemmas. (4) Independent hand check of C5[K4]: dist_even = 9 at every vertex; b = f = 4 (at most 2 vertices per block, a block with 2 forces empty neighbouring blocks, and one vertex per block gives an induced C5); bound 5 > 4. C5[K2] and C5[K3] satisfy the bound (4 ≤ 4), so the counterexample is not an artifact of the formalization. Status: the WOWII page still marks 63 'O' (open) in the July 2026 capture, but that page was last updated in 2020. The file's `research solved` / `answer(False)` rests on a verified formal disproof, so the file is ahead of the source rather than stale. I did not list this as a status issue. The cited URL is currently unreachable; the Wayback captures above preserve the content.
